solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shrub is a little dear, but useful

indicators.note: only a small part of the following phrase is wanted, so look inside its run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of dear, all of but, and the start of useful

explanation.surface: Someone praises a small plant as charming and practical too.
explanation.definitionFit: The arbutus, or strawberry tree, is an evergreen bush or small tree with red berries.

clue.text: Geography book finally abridged

indicators.note: an abridged text has been cut short, so the phrase loses its final letter

blocks.note: finally means at last

explanation.surface: A school textbook on geography at last appears in a shortened edition.
explanation.walkthrough: AT LAST with its final T cut gives ATLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, the standard reference volume for studying places.

clue.text: Unacceptable apart from white?

blocks.note: first meaning: outside the bounds of decent behaviour
second meaning, read literally: further away than something pale, a whitish colour

explanation.walkthrough: The pale was originally a fenced boundary; the clue instead reads pale as an adjective meaning whitish, so the phrase becomes past the white.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes conduct so improper it lies outside any limits society will tolerate.

clue.text: Unproductive time up for body of soldiers

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: poor land or work is unproductive
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Time spent idly ends, and a squad of soldiers is roused.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a cavalry or armoured unit, a group of military personnel under one command.

clue.text: Reason fool blocks authority

indicators.note: something that blocks a passage sits in the middle of it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: having the say is having authority
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A foolish person stands in the way of those in power and of sensible thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanity is soundness of mind, and reason as a noun names that same rational mental faculty.

clue.text: Popular friend is about to blossom

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable or popular
bud is American slang for a pal

explanation.surface: A well-liked companion is on the verge of coming into their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant with flowers still closed in their buds is ready to open soon.

clue.text: Quickly I recollect Athens

indicators.note: read as re-collect, gathering the letters together again in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller swiftly brings memories of the Greek capital to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in haste means hurrying, so the phrase works as an adverb of speed.

clue.text: Here notices why table is splintered?

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase: the answer read as bullet in board explains the damage

blocks.note: first meaning: a place where announcements are pinned up
second meaning, split into words: a shot lodged in the wooden top

explanation.walkthrough: Board is an old word for table, and a bullet lodged in it would cause the splintering.
explanation.definitionFit: A noticeboard is a panel in a public place where memos, posters and announcements are displayed.

clue.text: Takes one’s time getting wife into awkward saddle

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
something awkward is clumsy and out of shape, so these letters need rearranging

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider dawdles while trying to lift their wife onto an ill-fitting saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle is to linger or move slowly, wasting minutes instead of hurrying along.

clue.text: Peremptorily announce one’s retirement as solicitor?

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase for the answer read literally

blocks.note: first meaning: state something dogmatically, brooking no argument
second meaning, read literally: a lawyer putting down their profession for good

explanation.walkthrough: A solicitor is a British lawyer; laying down a career means giving it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to issue orders or opinions in an authoritative, domineering way.

clue.text: Play area is mine, after polish

indicators.note: one word comes after the other, fixing the order of the two parts

blocks.note: to sand wood is to smooth or polish it
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A child claims the playground as theirs once the floor is buffed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpit is a low enclosure filled with sand where small children dig and play.

clue.text: Charm for short period

blocks.note: first meaning: a magic incantation
second meaning: a brief stretch

explanation.surface: A magic charm that works only for a little while.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a magical formula of words and a limited stretch of time or weather.

clue.text: Varying in quality, like a much-mended garment

blocks.note: first meaning: uneven, good in places and poor in others
second meaning, literally: covered in sewn-on pieces of cloth

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is the literal sense from which the figurative uneven one comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irregular or inconsistent is patchy, as is clothing repaired with many sewn squares.

clue.text: Make coffee and drink: cheers!

blocks.note: to perk coffee is to brew it in a percolator
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Brew a pot and have a cup: here's to you!
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers looks like a toast, but it is a verb: it lifts someone's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe becoming livelier or lifting the mood, as a happier person does.

clue.text: All present for this subject? On the contrary

definitions.text: All present for this subject? On the contrary

blocks.note: surface reading: a teacher taking a register, checking that every pupil has turned up for the lesson
setter's reading: flip present to its opposite, so this school subject is all about the past

explanation.walkthrough: Present is the trap: it is not attendance but the current time, and its contrary is the past.
explanation.definitionFit: History is the academic discipline that studies earlier events, everything that has already happened.

clue.text: Steamship’s touring lake in sequence

indicators.note: a ship touring goes all around something, so it surrounds the other piece

blocks.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
Lake Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A steamer cruises a lake, calling at ports one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A series is a run of related things that follow one another in order.

clue.text: Grimace as citrus stews

indicators.note: stewing mixes and breaks down ingredients, so the letters get jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook pulls a face as the oranges simmer in the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rictus is a fixed, gaping contortion of the mouth, like a frozen grin or snarl.

clue.text: Mistakenly hears these can’t get off the ground

definitions.text: these can’t get off the ground

indicators.note: something done mistakenly comes out wrong, so the letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone misunderstands what they are told about a project that never takes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheas are large flightless South American birds, related to ostriches, that cannot fly.

clue.text: Live, dressed as monk?

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase: the answer read as in habit

blocks.note: first meaning: dwell in a place
second meaning, split in two: wearing the robe a monk wears

explanation.walkthrough: A habit is the long robe worn by monks and nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to occupy it as a home, to dwell or reside there.

clue.text: Scavenger’s longing to be in hot area

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a yen is a yearning
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A carrion-eater craves somewhere sweltering to live.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is an African carnivore known for feeding on carcasses left by other predators.

clue.text: Among a number, approve memento

indicators.note: one thing among another is surrounded by it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: ten is a number
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: From several options, someone signs off on a keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a small keepsake or souvenir kept as a reminder of a person or event.

clue.text: With which striker bestows congratulations?

blocks.note: surface reading: a footballer who has scored is being praised by teammates
setter's reading: the striker is anyone who strikes, here hitting a friend between the shoulders in praise

explanation.walkthrough: Striker suggests football; here it simply means the person delivering a friendly blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a hearty pat between the shoulder blades, and figuratively any warm praise.

clue.text: Shame about the end of reverence and devoutness

indicators.note: going about something means going around it, so the outer word surrounds the other
only the final letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: it is a pity means it is a shame
the final letter of reverence

explanation.surface: It is a pity when reverence and devotion fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion, being dutiful and sincere in worship.

clue.text: Deputy is not quite upright

indicators.note: not quite complete means the word falls short by its final letter

blocks.note: standing means upright, on one's feet

explanation.surface: An assistant is not entirely honest or principled.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute who takes someone's place, just as a deputy acts for a superior.
